answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose outcomes are later verified by randomly selected, stake-bearing reviewers; a reviewer who approves a fraudulent result loses part of its bond. The protocol caps each identity’s influence, so creating a swarm of aliases does not multiply voting power without also funding many independent bonds. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital across identities and risk losing it when sampled reviewers expose the fraud—rather than gaining control by minting names as cheaply as quartz, ivory, or a relic.
